Modeling
A baseline and three model classes, each tuned on 2020–21
Model
Why include it
Tuned (validation PR-AUC) → chosen
Offense-only lookup
The bar to beat: “just know the crime type”
None
Logistic regression
Interpretable odds ratios; linear benchmark
L2 strength C ∈ {0.01 … 10} → 10 (flat above 0.1)
Random forest
Learns interactions; robust with little tuning
Depth {12, 24, none} × min leaf {2, 5, 50} → none, 5
Gradient boosting
Usually best on tabular data; native categories
Learning rate {0.05, 0.15} × leaves {31, 127} → 0.05, 31; trees by early stopping (1,315)
How we tuned: fit each setting on 400k training cases (2009–19), score on all of 2020–21, pick the best PR-AUC, then refit on 2009–21.
Why not SVM or k-NN: both scale poorly to a million rows and add no interpretability over these.

Evaluation · Method
Metrics chosen for triage, scored once on 2022–25
Metric
Question it answers
Why we use it
PR-AUC (primary)
Are cleared cases ranked at the top?
Only ~1 in 6 test cases is cleared; triage only uses the top of the list
Top-20% capture
Review the top fifth: what share of solvable cases do you see?
The triage use case, in one number
Within-offense AUC
Does it rank cases of the same crime?
Isolates what the model adds beyond the crime type
Calibration, Brier
Do “20%” predictions come true 20% of the time?
Needed before showing probabilities to anyone
ROC-AUC
Overall ranking
For comparison only; easy negatives inflate it
Test set
283,385 incidents from 2022–2025, untouched during tuning and scored once at the end.

Working the model’s top fifth of cases finds 67% of solvable cases, vs. 56% knowing only the crime type.

Stakeholder question
Method
Why this method
“Same crime: does reporting late, or no witness, hurt the odds?”
Logistic-regression odds ratios
Coefficients are effects with the offense held fixed: the exact comparison asked

Model-agnostic, on unseen future data, in PR-AUC units; one-hot columns moved together

Partial dependence on delay, by crime type
Shows the real shape; odds ratios assume a straight line
Not used: per-case explanations (SHAP). No one acts on a single case’s breakdown, and it could be read as a verdict on one victim’s case.

Interpretation · What drives clearance
Crime type sets the odds; reporting delay matters most after that
Same crime, different odds
10× later report: 0.60× odds. No witness: 0.69×. Family violence: 2.9×, since the victim usually knows the suspect.
SDS 336 · Austin crime reports · 10
Interpretation · The shape of the delay effect
The window is the same few hours, not the first minutes
~11% → 6%
property crime, reported at 4 h vs. 8 h
~54% → 38%
violent crime, same window
Delay = 0 (44% of reports) is highest partly because those are cases written up on the spot. It records how a case arrived.
So: report within hours, not tomorrow.
SDS 336 · Austin crime reports · 11
Discussion · Limitations
What the model can’t tell us, and the risk of using it
The label is a police outcome
“Cleared” includes exceptional clearances, and recording habits (zero delays, rounded times) are features. Part of what it learns is how APD records cases.
Associations, not causes
Late reports may also lack evidence or a suspect description. Reporting faster won’t make every case solvable.
Feedback-loop risk
If low scores mean less effort, those cases get solved even less, and the next model learns that. Audit by district; never auto-screen out.
Drift and compute shortcuts
Needs yearly recalibration. Tuned on a 400k sample with small grids; settings scored within ±0.01.

Discussion · Takeaways
Whether a case gets solved depends on how it reaches police
01
For investigators
A score at intake ranks cases usefully. Use it as one input, recalibrated yearly, audited by district.
67%
of solvable cases in the model’s top fifth
02
For victims and the public
Report within hours, not tomorrow. Predicted clearance drops by a third to a half after that.
4–8 h
when predicted clearance falls
03
For anyone modeling this
Test on future years, and learn the data’s recording habits: they are part of the signal.
